rating.verdict: A good budget spells deck: Bolt, Monastery Swiftspear and Guttersnipe hit hard, but the creatures are fragile and the deck runs out of gas against tuned decks.
strengths: Lots of cheap burn that also triggers its creatures
Can win quickly from an empty board with Guttersnipe and Thermo-Alchemist
weaknesses: Payoff creatures die to any removal
Runs out of cards in long games
Lifegain decks are a big problem

wins: Cast cheap burn every turn: each spell deals damage and also makes an Elemental token, untaps Thermo-Alchemist or triggers Guttersnipe, so the opponent burns from both sides.
plan: Monastery Swiftspear (haste, gets bigger with each spell) or Lava Spike.
Young Pyromancer or Thermo-Alchemist, then keep casting burn: Shock, Bolt, Play with Fire.
Guttersnipe turns every spell into 2 extra damage. Inferno Titan finishes the game.
keys: A 1/1 Elemental token for every instant or sorcery you cast.
Taps to deal 1 to each opponent and untaps whenever you cast an instant or sorcery.
2 damage to each opponent for every instant or sorcery.
3 damage split among targets when it enters and every time it attacks.
tips: Play the payoff creature first, then the spells, so each spell triggers it.
Use burn on blockers early and on the opponent’s face late.
Tormenting Voice discards an extra land to draw two cards.
Lava Spike only hits players: save it for face damage.
mulligan: Keep 2–3 Mountains with a 1–2 mana creature and burn. This deck runs well on few lands.
